## 2

I understand why you might be skeptical of institutions or official images, but the evidence that Earth is round is much broader than photographs from space. We can observe ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, measure Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, track time zones, navigate using satellites, and see different stars from different parts of the world. People and organizations in many countries, including ones that disagree with each other politically, have independently reached the same conclusion. Space photographs are one kind of evidence, not the only kind.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors mixed together. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky. That is why the sky usually looks blue, even when you are looking away from the Sun. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, which scatters much of the blue light away, leaving more red, orange, and pink light for us to see.

雨下了一整夜，城市像被一层透明的纱笼住。屋檐不断滴水，清脆的声音落在寂静的巷子里，仿佛有人轻轻敲着一面看不见的鼓。昏黄的路灯映在积水中，被来往的车轮揉成细碎的光。窗玻璃上爬满蜿蜒的水痕，远处偶尔传来汽车驶过的声响，随后又被雨幕吞没。屋里亮着一盏小灯，热茶冒出的白雾贴近掌心，让漫长而潮湿的夜晚多了一点安宁。
